summary: ℚ/ℤ-valued characters separate the points of (O/ℓ^r O)^1; as this module is killed by ℓ^r, every such character comes from an additive map u to ℤ/ℓ^r, and u∘c is automatically a continuous cocycle for (cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r))^{−e}, so the hypothesis h kills b.

steps.claim: To prove b = 0 it suffices that every additive map (O/ℓ^r O)^1 → ℚ/ℤ kills b: characters with values in ℚ/ℤ separate the points of an abelian group.

The module (O/ℓ^r O)^1 is killed by ℓ^r (nsmul_quot_eq_zero), so composing with the embedding ℤ/ℓ^r → ℚ/ℤ (QZ.ofZMod) is a bijection from the additive maps (O/ℓ^r O)^1 → ℤ/ℓ^r onto the additive maps (O/ℓ^r O)^1 → ℚ/ℤ (QZ.bijective_ofZMod_comp); hence it suffices that QZ.ofZMod (ℓ^r) (u(b)) = 0 for every additive u : (O/ℓ^r O)^1 → ℤ/ℓ^r.

For such u, u∘c is a continuous cocycle for (cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r))^{−e}: it is locally constant because c is (c lies in the Selmer module, k), and from the cocycle identity c(gh) = c(g) + cycChar Ω ℓ (g)^{−e}·c(h) of c (mem_selmerModule_iff) one gets u(c(gh)) = u(c(g)) + (cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) g)^{−e}·u(c(h)), because u takes values killed by ℓ^r, so u(cycChar Ω ℓ (g)·y) = cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) g·u(y) (map_cycChar_smul; tateTwist, cycInv and charRep unfolded). By h, u(b) = 0, so its image in ℚ/ℤ is 0.
